subject: Sustained completion outliers impacting Evergreen checkout - initial triage
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@evergreen-retail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@evergreen-retail.com
Date: 2028-07-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evergreen - sudden sustained completion delays impacting checkout

Hi Soojin,

Over the last 45 minutes we've seen sustained completion delays from Redwood for our checkout text-generation calls. Symptoms: p99 completion time jumped from ~180ms to ~2.3s, a small bump in 5xxs (~0.3% -> 2.1%), and overall throughput to our integration dropped ~12%. This started ~08:25 PDT and is still ongoing.

We rely on Redwood for our anti-fraud and upsell prompts during checkout; this latency is causing client-side timeouts and increased cart abandonment. We're running on the hosted API with model pinned to rwd-open-7b-prod.

Requests: can you confirm whether there are service-wide anomalies, known capacity limits hitting, or configuration changes that could explain a sudden long-tail of completions? We're ready to join a call. Proposed: 09:30 PDT war-room.

I've attached a small CSV with sample request IDs and timestamps.

Thanks,
Carlos
Senior Ops Manager
Evergreen Retail
[attachment: evergreen_request_samples.csv (text/csv)]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@evergreen-retail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-21T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evergreen - sudden sustained completion delays impacting checkout

Carlos — thanks for the heads up and the sample IDs. Joining the 09:30 PDT call now.

Immediate asks (we'll triage live):
- Can you confirm whether the affected requests include streaming responses or plain completion calls?
- The CSV is great; please also share one full request+response pair if possible (headers + body).

Initial plan:
1) Quick sanity check on routing and model variants (so we can rule out accidental fallback to a heavier variant).
2) Pull per-shard concurrency and queue-length metrics for your tenant over the last 2 hours.
3) Request Dev to look at KV cache eviction/lookup patterns and any recent autoscaler events.

I've looped in Dev to start raw telemetry review. I'll produce an executive summary after the first 60 minutes and suggest mitigations (canary shift, temporary capacity bump, or targeted routing).

Call details: https://zoom.redwood/evergreen-triage-20280721

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@evergreen-retail.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evergreen - sudden sustained completion delays impacting checkout

Quick triage notes from infra side (summary of first-pass analysis):

Observations:
- At 08:24 PDT we started seeing a steady rise in queue length for the tenant shard group serving EVG (shard-group-54). Queue depth peaked ~120 requests queued per worker, where the normal steady-state is ~12.
- Concurrency cap per worker reached the configured soft limit (concurrency=48) across 3 of 5 workers in the group; autoscaler did not add capacity because CPU utilization remained moderate (~60%) and the autoscaler policy uses aggregated latency signals, which didn't trigger immediately.
- KV cache miss rate spiked from 7% -> 43% around the same time; subsequent lookups caused additional cold path work.
- We saw transient GC pauses on one worker (worker-54b) that correlated with several outlier completions.

Preliminary root-cause hypothesis: a burst of mid-size requests caused rapid KV churn and pushed per-worker concurrency to soft caps, which created queuing; since the autoscaler decision window is conservative, we had a brief window where queueing accumulated and long-tail completions appeared.

Files attached for deeper analysis: diagnostic_dump_evergreen_20280721.zip (heap/threads/trace), evg_pod_metrics_20280721.png (per-shard queues and concurrency).

Immediate mitigations put in motion:
- Increased soft concurrency limit for shard-group-54 from 48 -> 64 (temporary change, applied 10:40 PDT).
- Enabled a targeted autoscaler override for EVG for the next 3 hours to be more sensitive to queue depth.
- Flushed and warmed KV cache with sampled popular prefixes provided by Carlos.

Next steps:
- Run a controlled canary traffic shift for 20% of EVG traffic to a warmed pool with relaxed concurrency to measure impact.
- Follow-up: post-corroboration we'll revert temporary settings and propose longer-term changes (adjust autoscaler thresholds, improve cache prewarming for checkout routes).

Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@evergreen-retail.com>
Date: 2028-07-23T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Evergreen escalation: exec summary and ask

Team — following up with an executive summary for leadership ribbon-up. We completed the canary at 11:05 PDT on 2028-07-21 after Dev's temporary mitigations. Outcome: p99 fell back to ~210ms, 5xxs returned to baseline, and throughput restored to historical levels. Customer impact window was ~08:24 — 11:05 PDT.

Root cause (tl;dr): Rapid request burst + KV churn pushed per-worker concurrency to soft caps; autoscaler sensitivity to queueing was insufficient leading to transient queue buildup.

Customer-facing actions already completed:
- Warmed KV cache and shifted 20% of traffic to warmed pool (immediate).
- Increased soft concurrency and applied aggressive autoscaler override (temporary).
- Shared diagnostic bundle and timeline with EVG.

Proposed follow-up and asks for leadership approval:
1) Approve a short-term reserved burst capacity for Evergreen for the next 30 days (5 GPUs equivalent) while we implement autoscaler policy improvements. This avoids repeat impact and can be billed as a surge protection add-on; customer is requesting SLA credit for the impacted window.
2) Prioritize an autoscaler policy change to consider queue depth more aggressively for regional shards (target in the next sprint).
3) Formalize a KV prewarm contract for high-frequency checkout prefixes.

Questions for leadership:
- Approve CO-approved surge reserve (finance, sales) and guidance on issuing a partial credit for the ~2.75 hour customer impact window?

Carlos — we recommend a brief exec sync with Evergreen after you review the mitigation notes; we can propose the surge protection contract and a remediation timeline.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Success & Escalations
Redwood Inference
